  "text": "By morning Tobias had worn a pale place in the brim of his cap.

He sat in the last pew until the woman who cleaned the church asked whether he was waiting for someone. He said no. Then he asked her the time, though the clock was above the door and he had been watching it.

At nine he took the road to Maren's house.

There were gulls now. A van stood outside the bakery. Someone had put a broken chair beside a gate for anyone who wanted it.

Her door was shut.

He went round to the front window and cupped his hands against the glass. The lamp stood on the sill, unlit. Beyond it lay the rug, with one corner turned under. Maren always straightened that corner with her foot when she passed.

He knocked on the glass. His hands left two dull marks.

After a while he went to the porch. He had brought her key years ago, when her mother fell, and had never given it back. He found it in the little pocket inside his coat.

The key went in. He did not turn it.

From the other side came the small scrape of a chair being drawn towards the window.

Tobias took his hand away. The key remained in the lock.

On his way back he stopped beside the broken chair. One leg needed mending. He lifted it carefully and carried it home, keeping the loose leg still against his coat.",
